would_have_shipped_defects.evidence: verifier/registration-property.log:1 — "FAIL case 3: a REPLAYED emit against a run with events but no registry row did not register it — the open happens after the idempotency early-return"; artefacts/src/omegahive/gateway/gateway.py:99-102 (early return) vs :118-119 (open_run); artefacts/workspace.patch removes the RUNBOOK one-time `open_run` block.
would_have_shipped_defects.summary: The idempotent `open_run()` is placed after the idempotency-key early return in `Gateway.emit`, so a replayed emit against a run that has events but no registry row leaves the run unregistered.
would_have_shipped_defects.why_blocking: This is exactly the live `omegahive` situation the order exists to fix: a run with a full event history and no `runs` row. The order's registration path for the live run is "a side effect of the next real emit", and the attempt deleted the RUNBOOK's one-time `open_run` fallback, so registration now depends entirely on the emit path. Any emit carrying an idempotency key that has already been seen (the normal shape of an operator/worker re-drive after the restore this runbook governs) returns `Accepted(existing)` at gateway.py:102 and never reaches the `open_run()` at gateway.py:119. The operator then runs restore step 3's `bump-generation --run-id omegahive`, gets `run not registered`, and has no documented fallback — the caveat and the manual wiring one-liner were both removed. The inert durable signal the order was written to eliminate survives.

would_have_shipped_defects.evidence: verifier/registration-property.log:2 — "FAIL case 4: a run whose only emit was rejected carries no generation token"; artefacts/src/omegahive/gateway/gateway.py:107-111 and :161-176.
would_have_shipped_defects.summary: A run whose only emit is rejected records a `gateway.rejected` event but is never registered, so it carries no generation token.
would_have_shipped_defects.why_blocking: `_record_rejection` appends a real persisted event via `self._store.append` (gateway.py:161) and returns at gateway.py:111, before the `open_run()` at line 119. The order's scope item 1 is that "Every run touched by an emit then carries a generation token from its first event"; a run whose first event is a recorded refusal is touched by an emit, has an event, and still refuses `bump-generation`. Same operator-facing failure as above, on a second path.

would_have_shipped_defects.evidence: artefacts/docs/omegahive_recovery_runbook.md:90-92; artefacts/workspace.patch (RUNBOOK.md hunk deleting the caveat and the `open_run` one-liner); artefacts/workspace.patch report body, "What shipped" bullet 1 and "Reflection" bullet 2; contradicted by verifier/registration-property.log:1-3.
would_have_shipped_defects.summary: Both runbooks and the result report now assert unconditional registration that the shipped code does not deliver.
would_have_shipped_defects.why_blocking: The code-repo runbook tells the restoring operator "Runs are registered automatically when their first event is emitted; the durable `omegahive` project run is registered on its first emission", and the workspace RUNBOOK's caveat plus its reversible one-time `open_run` escape hatch are deleted. The report's What shipped repeats "every run touched by an emit carries a generation token from its first event" and its Reflection says "No manual intervention is needed once the code ships."
